tagline: Up the Big Wood, over Galena, down to the Sawtooths.
intro: Idaho 75 leaves Shoshone, an old railroad town set among lava rock, and climbs the Big Wood River valley through farmland to Bellevue, Hailey and Ketchum. North of Ketchum it runs under the Boulder Mountains, with peaks over 11,000 feet, and climbs to Galena Summit at 8,701 feet, the divide between the Big Wood and the Salmon.

A mile on, an overlook at 8,400 feet looks across to the Sawtooth range. The road comes down into the Sawtooth Valley and follows the headwaters of the Salmon north to Stanley, with the Sawtooths close on the west and the White Clouds farther off to the east.

moments.title: Shoshone Ice Caves
moments.text: About 15 miles north of Shoshone the ice in these lava tubes holds through the summer, and it once made the town the only place for hundreds of miles to get a cold beer.

moments.title: Ketchum
moments.text: By 1920 Ketchum was the largest sheep-shipping center in the West, and Hemingway, who later bought a house above the Big Wood River, is buried in its cemetery.

moments.title: Redfish Lake
moments.text: The lake is named for sockeye salmon that once came back from the Pacific in such numbers that it shimmered red at spawning time.
